content.title: About
content.content: Coleslaw is a classic salad made from finely shredded cabbage, carrots and onion, dressed with mayonnaise, sour cream or a vinegar‑oil dressing. It is a staple side dish in the United States and many other countries, often served with grilled meats and barbecues.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coleslaw originated in New England in the 19th century and quickly became a staple of American cuisine.
There are countless variations: some recipes add apple cider vinegar, mustard, honey or yogurt.
Traditional American coleslaw usually uses green cabbage, while many European versions favor red cabbage.
It is commonly served alongside fried chicken, fish, and sandwiches.
When stored properly, coleslaw can last up to 5 days, though the cabbage softens over time.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Cabbage provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad supplies vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism and blood formation.

items.title: Low calorie when dressed lightly
items.content: With a modest amount of dressing, coleslaw can be a light side dish with relatively few calories.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Cabbage contains vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: High fat content in dressing
items.content: Traditional mayonnaise‑based dressings add calories and saturated fat.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise contains eggs, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Some recipes include sugar or honey, raising the glycemic impact of the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coleslaw is served chilled as a side dish with barbecue, burgers, fish or fried chicken. It can also be added to sandwiches, tacos, or used as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store coleslaw in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. It keeps well for 3‑5 days. Before serving, stir to redistribute the dressing.
